Can someone explain how you make money off stock going down.

Most common ways.

1) Short selling the stock. AKA shorting. Sell stock (today) and at a future date buy back at a (hopefully) lower price. Requires broker to borrow the stock you sold which can require a fee(or income depending on borrowing demand).

2) Buying a put option on the stock. Option has the right to sell a specific amount of the stock at a future date. Sell ABC stock on Jun 15, 2017 for $50. Many dates and prices available. Can only lose cost of the option.

3) ETFs are available that short whole indexes. Beware of costs. Sometimes these ETFs don't mirror the exact underlying price movement.

There are many ways to short a stock but the two above are the most common.

Also, NEVER go long on an inverse ETF that is leveraged for long periods of time. It isn't obvious, but over time a leveraged ETF loses money.

you can see it mathematically by doing one fluctuation:

start with $100 in a 2x ETF
underlying goes down 10%, so the EFT goes up 20%
underlying goes up 11.11% (back to original), so the ETF goes down 22.22%
you end with $100 x 1.2 x 0.777 = $93.33

There are reasons not to long leveraged ETFs as well.

It'd be easier with charts and graphics but I'll try in words.

There are two main ways to make money from stock movements. Going "Long" and going "short."

You are familiar with "going long."

You buy something. You wait for its price to go up. You sell it. You pocket the difference.

There is another way to make money. Going short. It's difficult to imagine it with stocks... so let's use cars. And assume you have an extremely understanding friend.

Your friend has a 1997 Chevy Camaro. It's in good condition and worth $10,000. You ask him if you can borrow his car for a few weeks. He says: "sure. But you'll have to pay me some cash for the inconvenience."

You slip him $50.

You know your cars really well. And car prices move up and down a lot, in this world. For whatever reason you think the price of Camaro will fall so you sell your friend's car.

BLAM.

You have $10,000.

A few weeks pass and it's nearing time for you to give the car back to your friend as agreed.

You were clever. You knew the car market well. You were right - the price of Camaros has fallen.

You go to a used car lot and pick one up for $9000.

You give your friend this car you've just bought.

You get to pocket $10,000 minus the $9,000 for buying the car back minus the $50 you paid him at the start.

You made $950 off the price of cars falling.

TL;DR Sell for $10,000

Buy back for $9000

There's a $50 fee.

End result: You still have the stock plus $950 dollars: 10,000-(9000+50) = $950
Short version: find someone willing to bet that the stock will go up, and take their bet.
